draft.rationale: Recommend CONTEST: 3-D Secure authentication shifts fraud liability.

evidence.excerpt: AVS result Y, CVV result M
evidence.title: AVS / CVV

evidence.excerpt: For card-absent fraud disputes the cardholder states they did not authorise the purchase. The merchant can contest when the transaction was authenticated with 3-D Secure, because successful authentication shifts fraud liability to the issuer.
evidence.title: Network rules summary: card-absent fraud (Visa 10.4, Mastercard 4837)

evidence.excerpt: Without 3-D Secure authentication and without matching AVS and CVV results the merchant should normally accept the dispute and refund the cardholder, because a representment is unlikely to succeed.
evidence.title: Network rules summary: card-absent fraud (Visa 10.4, Mastercard 4837)

evidence.excerpt: Compelling evidence for card-absent fraud includes a full AVS match together with a CVV match, prior undisputed transactions on the same card from the same device or shipping address, and proof that the goods were delivered to the cardholder's billing address.
evidence.title: Network rules summary: card-absent fraud (Visa 10.4, Mastercard 4837)

evidence.excerpt: Orders above 250 USD are shipped with signature on delivery. For fraud disputes on 3-D Secure authenticated orders, Northwind contests by default.
evidence.title: Northwind refund and dispute policy

evidence.excerpt: For not-as-described disputes the cardholder states the goods differ from the description or are defective. The merchant should provide the product description shown at the time of sale and any customer communications.
evidence.title: Network rules summary: not as described or defective (Visa 13.3, Mastercard 4853)

evidence.excerpt: For merchandise-not-received disputes the cardholder states the goods never arrived. The merchant can contest only with proof of delivery: a carrier tracking record that shows the parcel delivered to the address the cardholder provided, with delivery date.
evidence.title: Network rules summary: merchandise not received (Visa 13.1)

evidence.excerpt: If the cardholder returned the item and the merchant received it, the merchant should refund in full.
evidence.title: Network rules summary: not as described or defective (Visa 13.3, Mastercard 4853)

queries: card-absent fraud 3-D Secure AVS CVV liability merchant policy
